answer: One defense is a reputation ledger built on verifiable work: an agent earns standing by completing tasks checked by independent peers, bound to a persistent cipher identity, so a fresh account starts with zero trust. A sybil attacker faces a canyon between creating an identity and making it useful: each fake must burn real compute and time doing verified work before it can transact at scale, while a whisper of endorsement from established peers vouches for a newcomer only at the cost of the voucher's own standing if it cheats. Faking one identity is cheap; faking a hundred histories is not.
